say.en: You have one evening and three things to do: revise, earn a little at a shop, or play a match. You cannot do all three. Economics begins with exactly this problem. In this lesson: Explain the wealth, welfare, scarcity and growth definitions of economics.
Relate scarcity to choice and opportunity cost.
Distinguish microeconomics and macroeconomics.

body.en: Adam Smith (1776) saw economics as the science of wealth: how nations produce and grow rich. Alfred Marshall (1890) shifted the focus to human welfare: the study of mankind in the ordinary business of life, especially material well-being. Lionel Robbins (1932) gave the scarcity *definition*: economics studies human behaviour as a relationship between ends and scarce means which have alternative uses. Paul Samuelson added growth: how society chooses to use scarce resources to produce goods over time and distribute them.

say.en: Robbins' definition has three parts.
On the board: Four definitions.

body.en: Human wants are unlimited and recur, while the means to satisfy them (land, labour, capital, time, money) are limited and have alternative uses. So every person, firm and government must choose. The value of the next best alternative given up is the *opportunity cost* of a choice. Microeconomics studies the choices of individual units such as a consumer or a firm; macroeconomics studies the economy as a whole: national income, employment and the price level.

points.en: Wants: unlimited; means: limited with alternative uses
*Opportunity cost*: the next best alternative forgone
Micro: parts of the economy; macro: the whole

problem.en: A farmer can use one hectare to grow rice worth ₹60,000, sugarcane worth ₹75,000 or vegetables worth ₹50,000. He chooses sugarcane. What is the opportunity cost of his choice?

steps.en: List the alternatives he gave up: rice (₹60,000) and vegetables (₹50,000).
Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative, not of all alternatives.
The next best is rice, worth ₹60,000.

answer.en: The opportunity cost of growing sugarcane is ₹60,000 (the rice forgone).
